new_findings.title: test_advance_gate_scripted_request_still_gated is vacuous — its assertion cannot fail if a scripted advance IGNORES the gate
new_findings.evidence: The test scripts Cmd_Era_Advance{to_era=3} at tick 100 under a healthy gate, runs 700 ticks, and asserts only s.era == 3 + !replay_error. Perkins code trace: an ungated scripted fire at tick 100 lands era 3; at era 3 the fixture's standard pipes are legacy (era 3 unlocks wide) blocking 3→4 forever — era==3 at tick 700 EITHER WAY. The Era_Advanced event's tick (600 gated vs 100 ungated) is collected but never asserted.
new_findings.detail: The only pin for the story-level contract 'a scripted advance still works, gated the same way' (PR body + stories-v2 6.2; the 6.1-mechanics-preserved headline on a win-condition canon surface) cannot fail under exactly the regression it guards. No golden covers scripted+gate-on (era_advance.dem is gate-off). Same vacuity class as r1's B2: a shipped guard that never guards.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Assert the Era_Advanced event tick >= milestone_window_ticks (600), or step only 500 ticks and expect era==2 with the latch held. Optionally add a scripted+gate golden.

new_findings.title: overlay_check's Demo_Replay literal omits advance_gate_on — the B1 flag-threading missed the third cfg site; the 3 gate demos re-sim gate-off in overlay renders
new_findings.evidence: cfg := Demo_Replay{ name/use_fixture/qos_fixture/session ... } — no advance_gate_on (demo_apply_setup then applies gate=false); the two other sites are fixed (run.odin:281 run_demo, run.odin:696 load_demo_replay).
new_findings.detail: The PP_DEBUG overlay-check verb on the 3 gate demos re-sims them with the gate disabled — the exported verification frame silently shows the wrong sim (no fire/block state). No golden/CI/app impact (gate 8 is compile-only) — the r1-B1 defect class, caught at its one residual site.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add advance_gate_on = d.advance_gate_on to overlay_check's cfg literal (one line, mirroring run.odin:281).

new_findings.title: W6 demand_era fold routed only the director — crisis/health(surge)/warnings still key demand rows by direct era-1 index (split-brain on divergent tables)
new_findings.evidence: demand.odin:59: de := &cat.demand.eras[dr.demand_era-1] (the fold); crisis.odin:337: de := &cat.demand.eras[state.era-1]; health.odin:117: de := &cat.demand.eras[era-1]; warnings.odin:239: de := &cat.demand.eras[state.era-1] — all three read the row the director no longer uses whenever demand_era != era.
new_findings.detail: The load-time invariant validates demand_era in-range but does not enforce identity, so a divergent (legal) era table makes the director read row demand_era while crisis/health/warnings read row era — inconsistent demand views within one run. Real catalog is identity (unaffected today); the r1-W6 fold is one-quarter landed at the reader level.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Route the three remaining readers through the era row's demand_era (or enforce eras[i].demand_era == i+1 at load and keep direct indexing everywhere).

new_findings.title: The new advance balance block parses via lenient jint — a decimal value silently truncates instead of failing fast
new_findings.evidence: b.advance.milestone_window_ticks = jint(aobj, ...) — jint accepts json.Float with i32(x) truncation (catalog.odin:1448-1456); jint_strict exists precisely because 'a decimal in the file is a fail-fast rejection ... the integer-only bar for the NEW catalogs' and is used 28x elsewhere; balance.json's own _comment declares 'All state-affecting values are int (ODN-10)'.
new_findings.detail: milestone_window_ticks: 600.5 loads as 600 and passes the 1..20000 check — an authoring foot-gun violating ODN-5's fail-fast bar for new tunables. Mitigation: consistent with balance.json's legacy loader convention (all jint); first-party content only.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Switch the two advance reads to jint_strict (rejecting decimals/out-of-i32/wrong types), matching the era/demand loaders.

new_findings.title: The W6 demand_era binding has no distinguishing test — only identity rows (demand_era == era) are ever exercised
new_findings.evidence: The existing demand-plan assertion (era 3's plan includes streaming) is an identity case (era 3 binds demand_era 3); the only divergent row (test-table era 4 → demand_era 3) is reached transiently by the crisis test's 3→4 fire but nothing asserts WHICH row era 4's plan reads.
new_findings.detail: The just-landed W6 fold can silently regress to direct indexing without any test failing (identity rows are index-insensitive). The fold's whole point — divergence correctness — is unpinned.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add a unit test: era 4's scripted_plan_demand must equal the demand_era-3 row's entries (fails if routed by era-1 index).

new_findings.title: Redundant era-table test scaffolding: era_test_catalog_3 rebuilds a table test_catalog already carries; era_test_catalog overwrites (and leaks) it
new_findings.evidence: test_catalog now builds era rows 1-3 (the W6 fixture fold); era_test_catalog_3 = era_test_catalog (rebuild 1-4, display strings differ) + pop → a semantically equivalent 3-row table; era_test_catalog's cat.eras = make(...) drops test_catalog's array without delete.
new_findings.detail: Dead-equivalent scaffolding whose comments claim it matters (the 'eras 1-3 only' call-site comments describe what already was true); two sources of truth for the test era table + a trivial fixture leak.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Delete era_test_catalog_3 (call era_test_catalog only where era 4 is needed); or make test_catalog the single table source.

new_findings.title: gate_record_run is a verbatim copy of the same-package era_record_run helper
new_findings.evidence: Both: hashes+events collection, start := s.tick + 1, per-tick batch from action_log, state_hash(s, s.events[before:], ...), clear + free_all — identical bodies.
new_findings.detail: Test-helper duplication in one package; the gate tests could use the existing helper.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Reuse era_record_run (or move one shared helper).

new_findings.title: The B2 fix's re-call pattern leans on an implicit invariant (replay_hashes reads the path before any free_all) rather than a stable lifetime
new_findings.evidence: replay_hashes(log_path(name), ...) — fresh temp string consumed at entry (run.odin:724 reads the file first); the comments document the ordering at both flip sites.
new_findings.detail: Probe-verified working; but a future replay_hashes change that allocates before the file read re-arms the vacuity silently. A strings.clone with context.allocator would be invariant-independent.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Clone the path with a stable allocator at the flip sites (belt-and-braces) or keep the documented ordering pin.

new_findings.title: `advance gate on` lacks the era>=1 parse-time cross-check `growth on` has — an era-0 gate demo would bless a silently-inert gate golden
new_findings.evidence: demo.odin:616: if d.growth_on && d.era == 0 { <reject> } — no analogous advance_gate_on check; the runtime comment instead documents 'the gate is inert ... at era 0 (no FSM)'.
new_findings.detail: Foot-gun guard only (the 3 real gate demos set era 2; runtime-inert is safe degradation) — but a typo'd gate demo at era 0 would bless a golden whose header claims gate coverage while never evaluating the gate (the mild cousin of r1's B1).
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add the sibling parse-time check: if d.advance_gate_on && d.era == 0 -> reject.

new_findings.title: Density check misses duplicate era rows — a duplicate silently overwrites and passes
new_findings.evidence: Rows store at index era-1; two {era:2} rows both write cat.eras[1] (last wins) — the dense check then sees 1,2 and passes; no duplicate detection anywhere in the eras load.
new_findings.detail: Authoring foot-gun; the surviving table stays semantically valid (one row wins), so impact is a silent content drop, not a runtime break.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Track seen era numbers (or compare row.era against the append index) and reject duplicates at load.

new_findings.title: Window-elapsed precondition duplicated with two tick sources (era_step's tick param vs era_gate_sla_ok's state.tick)
new_findings.evidence: era_step guards `tick < milestone_window_ticks`; era_gate_sla_ok re-checks `state.tick < milestone_window_ticks`; step.odin:56 sets state.tick = tick before era_step (:182) so they are equal today.
new_findings.detail: Harmless duplication today; a future caller divergence (param vs state) would desynchronize the precondition from the measurement.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Single-source the precondition (era_gate_sla_ok already checks it; drop one).

new_findings.title: Re-step hazard handled oppositely from the sibling growth feature — era_gate_update has no once-per-tick guard
new_findings.evidence: step gates growth on state.growth_last_tick != tick; era_gate_update double-invocation for one tick would zero the ring slot after subtracting it (win sums corrupted).
new_findings.detail: No reachable re-step path found (drivers step each tick once; replay re-sims fresh) — a defensive-consistency gap, not a live bug.
new_findings.recommended_fix: None required for 6.2; optionally mirror the growth guard for symmetry.

new_findings.title: Advance-block boundary values (window 20000, bar 1, bar 100) lack clean-load rows
new_findings.evidence: Rows cover missing/zero/negative/20001 for the window; no 20000-loads-clean row, no bar 1/100 clean rows (the 14400 row covers the documented mid-range).
new_findings.detail: Boundary-value hygiene; the cap arithmetic is trivial but unpinned at its edges.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add three clean-load rows (window 20000, bar 1, bar 100).
